title: Ensure root does not have ownership of Websphere Liberty binaries
description: Preventing the root user from owning files in the ${wlp.install.dir} directory prevents unauthorized commands or files from being run. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1 Ensure root does not have ownership of Websphere Liberty binaries

audit.command: Check to ensure that no files or directories underneath ${wlp.install.dir} are owned by the root user or root group: ls -l -R ${wlp.install.dir} | awk '{print $3, $4}' Expected result: You should not see the root user or root group referenced in the output.

remediation.command: Set the ownership and group of ${wlp.install.dir} to something other than root: chown -R <non-root user>:<non-root group> ${wlp.install.dir}

title: Ensure 'displayAuthenticationRealm' is set to 'false'
description: Configuring displayAuthenticationRealm will ensure that the registry information is not displayed in the login prompt. This will restrict the potential leak of security realm information. Audit: reads server.xml, configDropins/defaults/*.xml, configDropins/overrides/*.xml and files pulled in with <include> for every Liberty server found under WLP_USER_DIR, /opt/ibm/wlp/usr, /opt/IBM/WebSphere/Liberty/usr, /opt/ol/wlp/usr, /usr/local/wlp/usr or /config; it ignores XML comments and fails if no server.xml is readable. displayAuthenticationRealm must not be true. An unset attribute is accepted because the Liberty default is compliant.

'

title: Ensure that strong algorithms are used for TLS certificates.
description: Certificates created with stronger algorithms use stronger hashes which is more secure. Also, some browsers warn when using weak certificates. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.11 Ensure that strong algorithms are used for TLS certificates.

audit.command: Ensure that Signature algorithm name is SHA256 or higher and Subject Public Key Algorithm is equal or higher than 2048 bit. keytool -list -v -keystore <keystore file name> -storepass <store password> - storetype <store type> | grep 'Signature algorithm name\|Subject Public Key Algorithm' ... Signature algorithm name: SHA256withRSA Subject Public Key Algorithm: 2048-bit RSA key ...

remediation.command: Create certificates with SHA256 or higher algorithm and 2048 or higher key bit size.

title: Ensure that hardware crypto cards/modules (HSM) are used to store SSL/TLS certificates
description: Hardware security modules (HSMs) are hardened, tamper-resistant hardware devices that secure cryptographic processes by generating, protecting, and managing keys used for encrypting and decrypting data and creating digital signatures and certificates. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.13 Ensure that hardware crypto cards/modules (HSM) are used to store SSL/TLS certificates

audit.command: Ensure that the location attribute is set to the specific hardware crypto configuration file. In addition ensure that type attribute is set to PKCS11. Both these are under the keyStore element of the SSL configuration in the Liberty configuration. grep -w -R -i 'location' ${server.config.dir} grep -w -R -i 'type' ${server.config.dir}

remediation.command: Configure the location attribute to the specific hardware crypto card configuration file. In addition configure the type attribute to PKCS11. Both these attributes are in the keyStore element used by the SSL configuration in ${server.config.dir}/configDropins/overrides/*.xml. In this example, the HWCryto.cfg contains the hardware crypto configuration information. <keyStore id="hwKeyStore" location="${server.config.dir}/HWCrypto.cfg" type="PKCS11" fileBased="false" provider="IBMPKCS11Impl" ... />

title: Ensure SP800-131a recommendation is used for stronger cryptographic keys and more robust algorithms.
description: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) SP800-131a recommendation enforces stronger cryptographic keys and more robust algorithms. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.14 Ensure SP800-131a recommendation is used for stronger cryptographic keys and more robust algorithms.

audit.command: The SP800-131a recommendation can be enforced by setting the system property com.ibm.jsse2.sp800-131 to strict when using IBM JDK. For other JDKs, follow their specific instructions. Set com.ibm.jsse2.sp800-131=strict in the jvm.options file. More information on how to set the system properties provided in the reference section. grep -w -R -i 'com.ibm.jsse2.sp800-131=strict' ${server.config.dir}

remediation.command: Configure the system property -Dcom.ibm.jsse2.sp800-131 to strict in the jvm.options file. The link in reference section provides more information on how to customize the Liberty environment with system properties. In the jvm.options file add the following -Dcom.ibm.jsse2.sp800-131=strict ...

title: Ensure that the Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) are used for the cryptographic modules
description: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) issues the FIPS 140 Publication Series to coordinate the requirements and standards for cryptography modules that include both hardware and software components. Protection of a cryptographic module within a security system is necessary to maintain the confidentiality and integrity of the information protected by the module. This standard specifies the security requirements that will be satisfied by a cryptographic module. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.15 Ensure that the Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) are used for the cryptographic modules

audit.command: The FIPS standard can be enforced by setting the system properties - Dcom.ibm.jsse2.usefipsprovider=true and - Dcom.ibm.jsse2.usefipsProviderName=IBMJCEPlusFIPS when using IBM JDK. For other JDKs, follow their specific instructions. grep -w -R -i '-Dcom.ibm.jsse2.usefipsprovider=true' ${server.config.dir} grep -w -R -i '-Dcom.ibm.jsse2.usefipsProviderName=IBMJCEPlusFIPS' ${server.config.dir} In addition, configure to use the IBMJCEPlusFIPS security provider in the $JAVA_HOME/jre/lib/security/java.security file. grep -w -R -i 'com.ibm.crypto.plus.provider.IBMJCEPlusFIPS' ${JAVA_HOME}

remediation.command: Configure the system property -Dcom.ibm.jsse2.usefipsprovider to true and - Dcom.ibm.jsse2.usefipsProviderName to IBMJCEPlusFIPS in the jvm.options file. The link in reference section provides more information on how to customize the Liberty environment with system properties. -Dcom.ibm.jsse2.usefipsprovider=true -Dcom.ibm.jsse2.usefipsProviderName=`IBMJCEPlusFIPS` ... In addition, configure the IBMJCEPlusFIPS provider in the $JAVA_HOME/jre/lib/security/java.security file. security.provider.1=com.ibm.crypto.plus.provider.IBMJCEPlusFIPS ...

title: Ensure Web Server Document Root does not contain information that should be private
description: WAR files contain servable content. The Web container will serve any files found in the root(Web Server Document Root) of the WAR file. This is fine as long as you place only servable content in the root. Thus, you should never place content that shouldn't be shown to users in the root of the WAR. For example, don't put property files, class files, or other important information there. If you must place such information in the WAR file, place it within the WEB-INF directory, as permitted by the servlet specification. Information there is never served by the Web. TMAegis cannot evaluate this reliably, so it is reported as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.4.15 Ensure Web Server Document Root does not contain information that should be private

audit.command: Ensure that there is no content that shouldn't be shown to users in the root of the WAR. For example, check for property files, class files, or other important information.

remediation.command: Remove all content that shouldn't be shown to users in the root of the WAR. For example, relocate property files, class files, or other important information within the WEB-INF directory, as permitted by the servlet specification.

title: Ensure extraneous files and directories are removed
description: The installation might provide example applications, documentation, and other directories which may not serve a production use. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2 Ensure extraneous files and directories are removed

audit.command: Check for the existence of extraneous resources: $ ls -l ${wlp.user.dir}/extension \ ${wlp.user.dir}/shared \ ${wlp.user.dir}/server \ ${wlp.user.dir}/client There should be no non-production client extension/shared resource(s)/server/client in these folders

remediation.command: Remove extraneous resources for each: Extension: $ rm -rf ${wlp.user.dir}/extension/<non-production extension> Shared resource(s): $ rm -rf ${wlp.user.dir}/shared/<non-production shared resource(s)> Server: $ rm -rf ${wlp.user.dir}/server/<non-production server> Client: $ rm -rf ${wlp.user.dir}/client/<non-production client>

title: Ensure only defined users have access to the file system
description: In Linux systems, there is a category of permission as others. These users are the ones who are not neither owner nor in a group associated with the file/folder. Since these users are anyone else than users defined, they should not have any access at all on Websphere Liberty file system. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3 Ensure only defined users have access to the file system

audit.command: Ensure that no one falling into other category have access to the Websphere Liberty file system. You should expect to see ---. ls -l -R ${wlp.install.dir} | awk '{print substr($1,length($1)-3,3)}'

remediation.command: Ensure that other has no access to the system. chmod -R o-rwx ${wlp.install.dir}

title: Ensure that only one user ID has write access to the WebSphere Liberty configuration files
description: Ensure that only one user ID has write access to the WebSphere Liberty configuration files. If there are multiple administrators, they can use sudo and the /etc/sudoers file to elevate their privilege when write access is required. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4 Ensure that only one user ID has write access to the WebSphere Liberty configuration files

audit.command: Verify that all WebSphere administrators have been added to the group that owns the server's configuration directory, which will grant them read but not write access. Ensure that the user that owns the server's configuration directory is a non-login user. Use sudo and the /etc/sudoers file to grant the administrators the ability to elevate their privilege to the user that owns the server's configuration directory when write access is required.

remediation.command: Create a single, non-login, user ID that owns the server's configuration directory. Add any WebSphere administrators to the group that owns the server's configuration directory, which will automatically give them read access to the server's configuration, but not write access. Use sudo and the /etc/sudoers file to allow these administrators to elevate their privilege to the user ID that owns the server's configuration directory when write access is required.

title: Ensure Websphere Liberty Server Output is not set to the default value
description: The user ID that the WebSphere Liberty server process runs under should not have write access to its own configuration files. The WebSphere Liberty server process requires write access to certain runtime files such as temporary caches and logs, but those files can be written to a different location than the configuration files, and permissions can be set separately for those two locations. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5 Ensure Websphere Liberty Server Output is not set to the default value

audit.command: Ensure the existence of the WLP_OUTPUT_DIR variable in the server.env file. This environment variable is used to specify an alternative location for server generated output such as logs, the workarea directory, and other generated files. The variable should point to an output directory that is different from the server's configuration directory. The user ID of the WebSphere Liberty server process should have write access to the output directory but only read access to the configuration directory. For more information about server.env please see here. ...

remediation.command: Create the server.env file if it does not exist. For more information about server.env please see here. Define WLP_OUTPUT_DIR in the server.env file: WLP_OUTPUT_DIR=/<server-writeable directory>/ Ensure that the WebSphere Liberty server process user ID has write access to the WLP_OUTPUT_DIR directory. Ensure that the WebSphere Liberty server process user ID does not have write access to the ${server.config.dir} directory.

title: Ensure the WebSphere Liberty Installation is Validated
description: Ensure that all WebSphere Liberty binaries were installed successfully and that you are running the latest fix pack version. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7 Ensure the WebSphere Liberty Installation is Validated

audit.command: Validate your WebSphere Liberty installation by running the command below: ${wlp_install_dir}/bin/productInfo validate Expected result: Start product validation... Product validation completed successfully. Validate that you are running with the latest fixpack. ${wlp_install_dir}/bin/productInfo version Expected result: Product version: YY.0.0.FP In the output, YY is the last two digits of the year that the fixpack was released, and FP represents the fixpack number for that year. Ensure that this matches that latest fixpack available from IBM.

remediation.command: If the audit procedure fails, remove your current installation and install from a more secure location, ensuring that you are installing the latest fixpack from a trusted source.

title: Ensure Websphere Liberty file system access is Restricted
description: The permissions of files and directories underneath ${wlp.install.dir} should follow the principle of least privilege. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.8 Ensure Websphere Liberty file system access is Restricted

reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.4 Ensure the 'addressIncludeList' attribute is set to a whitelist of IP addresses

audit.command: Ensure the addressIncludeList attribute is set to a list of IP addresses in all tcpOptions elements in the Liberty configuration. grep -w -R -i 'addressIncludeList' ${server.config.dir}

remediation.command: Add the addressIncludeList attribute to all tcpOptions elements to ${server.config.dir}/configDropins/overrides/*.xml and set to comma-separated list of IP Address. <tcpOptions addressIncludeList="254.*.*.9,255.0.0.2" />

title: Ensure 'zosSecurity-1.0' feature is 'enabled' for SAF authorization
description: The SAF role mapper should be used to perform SAF authorization checks when accessing applications. Requires the zosSecurity-1.0 feature and a <safAuthorization> element.

'

[ -f /config/server.xml ] && r="$r/config/$nl"
strip(){ awk 'BEGIN{RS="<!--"} NR==1{printf "%s",$0; next} {i=index($0,"-->"); if(i) printf "%s",substr($0,i+3)}'; }
gather(){ s=$1; { cat "${s}server.xml" "${s}"configDropins/defaults/*.xml "${s}"configDropins/overrides/*.xml; } 2>/dev/null | strip
  for loc in $(cat "${s}server.xml" "${s}"configDropins/defaults/*.xml "${s}"configDropins/overrides/*.xml 2>/dev/null | strip | tr '\r\n\t' '   ' | grep -oE '<include[[:space:]][^>]*>' | sed -n 's/.*location[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p'); do
    case $loc in http*) continue;; esac; loc=$(printf '%s' "$loc" | sed "s#\${server.config.dir}/*##"); case $loc in /*) f=$loc;; *) f=$s$loc;; esac
    [ -f "$f" ] && strip < "$f"; done; }

  [ "$st" -lt "$tot" ] && [ "$4" != y ] && return 1; return 0; }
IFS="$nl"; for s in $r; do n=$((n+1)); X=$(gather "$s" | tr '\r\n\t' '   ' | tr -s ' ')

title: Ensure Unused Features are Removed
description: The Websphere Liberty architecture provides developers with the option to tune their server to only the features that they need. For example, the JDBC feature only needs to be added if database access is required. If you did not want any remote administrative access to the REST interface, you would remove the REST feature. TMAegis cannot evaluate this reliably, so it is reported as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 10.1 Ensure Unused Features are Removed

audit.command: Review the configuration for features not being used in Liberty configuration. This includes aggregated features containing multiple features. The features are listed under in the featureManager element. To review all of the individual features used in the server, review the messages.log for the CWWKF0012I message. grep -w -R -i CWWKF0012I ${server.config.dir}

remediation.command: Removed any unneeded features listed under the featureManager element in the Liberty configuration

title: Ensure that constrained delegation is configured for SPNEGO (Simple and Protected GSSAPI Negotiation Mechanism)
description: SPNEGO authentication supports both constrained and unconstrained delegation. Constrained delegation provides the ability to specify and enforce application trust boundaries on a user's behalf by limiting the flow of the SPENGO tokens only to trusted servers. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual; TMAegis reports it as a manual review item with the audit steps.
reference: CIS IBM WebSphere Liberty Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.3.2 Ensure that constrained delegation is configured for SPNEGO (Simple and Protected GSSAPI Negotiation Mechanism)

audit.command: If SPNEGO authentication is configured in the Liberty server make sure that the constrained delegation feature is also enabled in the Liberty configuration. grep -w -R -i 'spnego' ${server.config.dir} grep -w -R -i 'constrainedDelegation' ${server.config.dir}

remediation.command: In ${server.config.dir}/configDropins/overrides/<any file name>.xml, add the constrainedDelegation-1.0 feature to the featureManager element: <feature>constrainedDelegation-1.0</feature>
